extracted.intended_audience: Prospective and current IEEE peer reviewers (researchers, academics, industry scientists) who will evaluate submitted manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for serving as a peer reviewer for IEEE journals: how to sign up, the peer-review process structure, section-by-section standards for manuscripts, ethical obligations, how to write reviews, and recommendation categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer signup and expertise matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an account on the publication's submission site and select keywords matching your expertise to enter the reviewer pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement to ensure reviewers are matched to appropriate manuscripts; selecting specific keywords is required to be considered for review invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number and independence of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: "At least two independent, qualified reviewers" evaluate articles after prescreening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is conducted by a minimum of two independent reviewers; this occurs following an initial prescreening step by the editorial office or editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to the field and novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: "Contribution to the field and novelty" — assess whether the manuscript advances knowledge and presents novel work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate originality and significance: does the paper add new insights or capabilities relative to existing literature?

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature review completeness and reference appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature review completeness and reference appropriateness — check that related work is cited and referenced appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for missing key references, inappropriate citations, or lack of engagement with prior art; references should be relevant and balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology soundness and experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology soundness and experimental design — determine whether the methods are appropriate and robust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether study design, algorithms, experiments, or analyses are suitable to support the claims and whether controls, baselines, and evaluation metrics are adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Result quality, clarity, and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Result quality, clarity, and reproducibility — evaluate how results are presented and whether they can be reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for clear presentation of results, availability of data/code if required, sufficient detail to reproduce experiments, and honest reporting of limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical conclusions and organizational flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical conclusions and organizational flow — verify that conclusions follow from results and that the manuscript is well organized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure arguments are coherent, claims are supported by evidence, and the paper structure aids comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract: ≤250 words, self-contained, accurately reflects content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should summarize purpose, methods, main results, and conclusions within the word limit and without requiring the reader to consult the full text for basic understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction: establishes context and research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The introduction should motivate the problem, place it in context, state the gap in knowledge, and clearly articulate research objectives or questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology section standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology: detailed and reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods should be described with enough detail that another competent researcher could reproduce the work; include parameter settings, datasets, algorithms, and statistical procedures as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results section standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Results: appropriately analyzed and presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results must be analyzed using appropriate techniques, clearly reported (tables/figures labeled), and include measures of uncertainty or statistical significance where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion section standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion: addresses research questions, highlights significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion should interpret results in the context of the research questions, compare with prior work, explain implications, and acknowledge limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusion: supported by findings only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions must be grounded in the presented results and avoid overstating or making unsupported claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: References quality
rubrics_metrics.description: References: relevant, recent, balanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations should include pertinent recent work and represent the field fairly; avoid omission of key literature or excessive self-citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report plagiarism and duplicate publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Author misconduct to report: Plagiarism, duplicate publication, parallel submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If detected, notify editors; these practices violate publication ethics and should trigger editorial investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report data fabrication or image manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Author misconduct to report: Data fabrication or image manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspected falsification or manipulation of results/images must be reported to editors with supporting evidence or explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report inappropriate authorship and citation stacking
rubrics_metrics.description: Author misconduct to report: Inappropriate authorship, citation stacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report cases of improper attribution of authorship (ghost/gift authorship) or coordinated citation practices intended to game metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain manuscript confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer misconduct to avoid: Breaching confidentiality or contacting authors directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share manuscript content or discuss it outside the review process; all communications must go through the editorial system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid citation coercion and undisclosed conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer misconduct to avoid: Citation coercion or conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pressure authors to add citations for reviewer benefit; disclose any conflicts that could bias your review and recuse if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure — concise summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Review writing structure: 1. Summary of purpose and findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin reviews with a brief, neutral summary demonstrating understanding of the manuscript's aims and main results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure — major concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Review writing structure: 2. Major concerns (methodology, data, analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and explain substantive problems that affect the validity or integrity of the work; be specific about what must change to address issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure — minor concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Review writing structure: 3. Minor concerns (clarity, structure, presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note issues that improve clarity or presentation (typos, figure labeling, small rephrasings) that do not undermine the main findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure — overall feedback and recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Review writing structure: 4. Overall feedback with recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear overall assessment and explicit recommendation category, summarizing whether the paper should be accepted, revised, or rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using AI to draft reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical Restrictions: "Do **not** use AI tools...to generate or draft reviews".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review text must be the reviewer's own work; do not rely on generative AI to produce review content or substantive judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline review if conflicts exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical Restrictions: Decline if conflicts of interest exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a conflict (financial, personal, competitive), you must decline the invitation so an unbiased reviewer can be assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest references only with justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical Restrictions: Only suggest relevant references with justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing additional citations, explain why they are required and how they relate to the manuscript; avoid self-serving suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain strict confidentiality of unpublished content
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical Restrictions: Maintain strict confidentiality of unpublished content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use or disclose ideas, data, or methods from the manuscript for your own work until it is published; maintain confidentiality throughout the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation category — Accept
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: Accept — Meets standards with no changes required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the manuscript satisfies the journal's quality, novelty, and ethical standards and requires no revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation category — Revise
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: Revise — Major or minor revisions needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the manuscript has merit but requires changes; specify whether issues are major (affecting validity) or minor (presentation, clarification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation category — Reject
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: Reject — Fundamental issues present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the manuscript has serious flaws in approach, novelty, ethics, or presentation that are unlikely to be remedied by revision.
